Prevention: Destruction of alternate host plants e.g. tomato, potato, pepper, Musa spp., Sugar, apple etc. before sowing.
The mealybugs can survive for weeks on crop debris and in egg masses that have fallen off plants.
So removal of crop debris is the best prevention for mealybug.
Keep the water channels clean from weeds throughout the growing season.
Disinfect tools and containers with one part bleach in four parts water or with 70 % rubbing alcohol (isopropyl).
Avoid movement of infested plant material within the growing area.
Appropriate nutrition, water, growing media and other conditions should be ensured as weak plants are more susceptible to damage at lower populations of pests.
Monitoring: Monitor on alternate host plants initially and later on the crop two weeks after transplantation twice a week.
Observe the oval rounded body with light orange to pink colour, monitor the eggs and flaments of the body.
Be prepared when the temperature is 35-40 °C and
RH 60-70% as these are optimal conditions for the mealybugs.
They can survive for weeks on crop debris and in egg masses that have fallen off plants.
Initially attack appears on folliage and fruit.
Monitoring includes visual observations, turning over leaves, looking for black sooty mould and the presence of ants on plants.
Direct Control: Uproot the infested plants and bury in ground.
Observe the presence of predators like greenlacewing and lady bird beetles.
Avoid application of pesticides when reasonable levels of natural enemies are present in the field.
Control ants as they spread crawlers and protect mealybugs from natural enemies.
Restrictions: Always wear impermeable gloves, long pants & long-sleeve shirts during spray
Change clothes and wash your hands immediately after applying pesticides.
Don't spray outdoors on windy or rainy days.
Tagging and spot spraying with above mentioned pesticides if attack is in patches.
